newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Surcharges breach Rome Treaty - Dutch airshippers.
newsitem.headline: Surcharges breach Rome Treaty - Dutch airshippers.

text.p: Airlines which introduced cargo surcharges this month in response to high jet fuel prices are in breach of the Treaty of Rome, the Dutch shippers association EVO said in a statement.

EVO, which represents manufacturers and exporters, added that it has lodged a formal complaint with the Dutch Minister of Economic Affairs Hans Wijers and it is seeking to have the surcharges declared illegal.

Hans Leijgraaff, secretary of the air shippers group at EVO, told Reuters: "We're looking to the minister for condemnation of the surcharges and we want him to declare them to be illegal as they have been introduced in a co-ordinated manner, not just in the Netherlands but throughout Europe."
The ministry said it had received the complaint, but said it was too early to comment.

EVO said it was seeking legal advice on the matter and could prove that the surcharges contravene Articles 85.1 and 85 of the Rome Treaty, which govern fair trading practices in European Union countries.

Leijgraaff said in a telephone interview: "Shippers have their backs to the wall. Because the surcharges are so co-ordinated, there is no option to switch to other forms of transport or to other carriers. They have no competitive alternative."

EVO's statement said Dutch shippers were being placed under extreme financial duress by the surcharges and Leijgraaff added: "It is clear that our shippers are not alone. The same problems are being felt all over Europe."
The organisation represents some 40,000 Dutch shippers who move goods using a range of transport methods.
